questions.question: What is the primary difference between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and pretraining for large language models?
questions.choice_A: SFT optimizes on supervised input–output pairs, whereas pretraining optimizes next-token prediction on unlabeled text
questions.choice_B: SFT uses reinforcement learning signals, whereas pretraining uses supervised gradients
questions.choice_C: SFT only updates the output layer, whereas pretraining updates all layers
questions.choice_D: SFT requires significantly larger datasets than pretraining

questions.question: Which data collection strategy most directly supports instruction tuning’s goal of generalizing to new tasks?
questions.choice_A: Collecting large amounts of single-domain supervised pairs
questions.choice_B: Curating diverse, multi-domain instruction–response pairs with varied phrasing and solution styles
questions.choice_C: Sampling only from high-resource benchmarks to maximize quality
questions.choice_D: Focusing on tasks where the model already performs well to stabilize training

questions.question: In instruction tuning, why is including multiple prompt formats for the same task beneficial?
questions.choice_A: It increases the model’s vocabulary size
questions.choice_B: It ensures the model learns to ignore instructions and rely on priors
questions.choice_C: It reduces overfitting to a specific template and improves robustness to prompt variations
questions.choice_D: It guarantees state-of-the-art performance on all downstream tasks

questions.question: Which initialization strategy typically yields the strongest performance for SFT on instruction data?
questions.choice_A: Training from scratch on the instruction dataset
questions.choice_B: Initializing from a domain-specific small model
questions.choice_C: Initializing from a large, general-purpose pretrained LM and then fine-tuning
questions.choice_D: Randomly initializing only the final layer and freezing all others

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when evaluating instruction-tuned models solely on held-out prompts that share the same format as training data?
questions.choice_A: Underestimating compute costs
questions.choice_B: Overestimating generalization due to format overfitting
questions.choice_C: Underestimating model size requirements
questions.choice_D: Missing gains from larger batch sizes

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes instruction tuning from standard SFT on task-specific data?
questions.choice_A: Instruction tuning uses natural language instructions across many tasks, aiming for broad generalization rather than optimizing one task
questions.choice_B: Instruction tuning always requires RLHF after SFT
questions.choice_C: Instruction tuning does not update model weights
questions.choice_D: Instruction tuning relies on synthetic data only

questions.question: When continually fine-tuning a model on new instruction datasets, what risk must be explicitly managed?
questions.choice_A: Vanishing gradients due to short sequences
questions.choice_B: Catastrophic forgetting of earlier capabilities
questions.choice_C: Exploding vocabulary size
questions.choice_D: Deterministic decoding across all temperatures

questions.question: Which evaluation design best probes generalization to unseen instructions?
questions.choice_A: Testing on the same tasks with lightly paraphrased prompts
questions.choice_B: Testing on held-out tasks with new instruction styles and different input distributions
questions.choice_C: Testing on the training set with nucleus sampling
questions.choice_D: Testing only with zero-shot chain-of-thought prompts

questions.question: Why might a model fine-tuned heavily on a single instruction template perform poorly when users deviate from that template?
questions.choice_A: The tokenizer cannot encode new templates
questions.choice_B: The optimizer discourages new formats
questions.choice_C: The model has learned spurious correlations between format cues and outputs
questions.choice_D: The model’s attention heads become permanently fixed

questions.question: Which approach is most appropriate for low-resource SFT to preserve base model capabilities while adapting to new instructions?
questions.choice_A: Full-model fine-tuning with a high learning rate
questions.choice_B: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., adapters or LoRA) with careful regularization
questions.choice_C: Training only the embedding layer
questions.choice_D: Freezing all layers and updating only the tokenizer

questions.question: What is an advantage of including both positive and negative examples in instruction-tuning data?
questions.choice_A: It simplifies the loss function to a margin loss
questions.choice_B: It helps the model learn what not to do and calibrates refusals and constraints
questions.choice_C: It removes the need for evaluation on safety benchmarks
questions.choice_D: It eliminates distribution shift issues

questions.question: Which statement best describes the SFT objective typically used for instruction tuning?
questions.choice_A: Maximize reward from a human preference model
questions.choice_B: Minimize KL divergence to the base model
questions.choice_C: Minimize cross-entropy loss on reference responses conditioned on instructions and inputs
questions.choice_D: Maximize mutual information between instruction and response embeddings

questions.question: What is a recommended practice to reduce data contamination risks when evaluating instruction-tuned models?
questions.choice_A: Use only synthetic benchmarks generated by the model itself
questions.choice_B: Ensure strict dataset de-duplication and provenance checks against training corpora
questions.choice_C: Use longer generation lengths during evaluation
questions.choice_D: Freeze the model’s positional embeddings

questions.question: Why can mixing multi-turn dialogues with single-turn instruction pairs be beneficial during SFT?
questions.choice_A: It guarantees lower perplexity on all tasks
questions.choice_B: It helps the model learn conversational state and follow-up instruction handling
questions.choice_C: It decreases the need for context windows
questions.choice_D: It forces the model to ignore earlier turns

questions.question: What is a robust evaluation signal that a model has truly learned instruction following rather than memorizing templates?
questions.choice_A: High accuracy on the training templates
questions.choice_B: Stable performance when the same task is rephrased with different directives and constraints
questions.choice_C: Lower loss on longer sequences
questions.choice_D: Increased token diversity in outputs

questions.question: Which of the following is a realistic sign of overfitting during instruction SFT?
questions.choice_A: The model performs well on both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks
questions.choice_B: Validation loss on held-out templates decreases while performance on new instruction styles stagnates or drops
questions.choice_C: Perplexity increases on the training set
questions.choice_D: The model’s output length becomes more variable

questions.question: How can one mitigate catastrophic forgetting when continually fine-tuning on new instruction data?
questions.choice_A: Use only higher learning rates
questions.choice_B: Apply rehearsal (mixing prior data), regularization to the base model (e.g., KL or L2), or parameter-efficient layers
questions.choice_C: Shorten all sequences during training
questions.choice_D: Disable dropout

questions.question: What is a key concern when using synthetic instruction–response data generated by an LLM for SFT?
questions.choice_A: Synthetic data cannot be tokenized
questions.choice_B: It may propagate model biases or errors, requiring filtering and diversity controls
questions.choice_C: It removes the need for human oversight
questions.choice_D: It forces the model to underfit

questions.question: Which metric or protocol best assesses instruction adherence rather than pure task accuracy?
questions.choice_A: BLEU against reference answers only
questions.choice_B: Human or rubric-based evaluation scoring compliance with constraints, steps, and style
questions.choice_C: Perplexity on the instruction text
questions.choice_D: Top-k diversity of generated tokens

questions.question: What is a typical symptom of distribution shift between SFT training and deployment contexts for an instruction-tuned model?
questions.choice_A: Improved calibration under temperature 0
questions.choice_B: Failure to follow instructions that include unseen constraints or domains
questions.choice_C: Reduced inference latency
questions.choice_D: Lower memory usage during decoding
